name: WACO F-series / UPF-7 open-cockpit biplane
variants: F-series sport biplanes (INF, RNF, UBF, UMF, QCF)
summary: Open-cockpit 1930s sport and primary-training biplane; the UPF-7 became a Civilian Pilot Training Program workhorse and many survive as show and airshow aircraft.

wings: Staggered biplane with a single bay of interplane struts and flying wires
Wings are rounded at the tips with ailerons on the wings
engines: Radial engine (Continental, Jacobs, Warner or Kinner) in the nose, often with a partial or ring cowl
fuselage: Tandem open cockpits with a wide front cockpit that seats two passengers
Wide-track fixed tailwheel gear, often with wheel pants
tail: Rounded fin and rudder (enlarged on later YMF)

tellTales: Open-cockpit biplane with a wide front cockpit seating two side by side
Radial-engined biplane with a smooth, streamlined fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Stearman has a larger, bulkier airframe with narrow tandem cockpits and a bare radial; the Waco's front cockpit is wide and its fuselage is smoother and slimmer.
The Waco 10 family is the earlier barnstormer with a water-cooled OX-5 radiator on many examples and a more upright, slab-sided look; the F-series is later and more streamlined.
The Travel Air 2000 has big 'elephant-ear' ailerons with overhanging horns; the Waco F-series ailerons are conventional.
The Taperwing has wings that visibly taper toward the tips; the F-series wings are untapered with rounded tips.
